newsitem.title: UK: WORLD BONDS-US poll likely to leave T-bonds cold.
newsitem.headline: WORLD BONDS-US poll likely to leave T-bonds cold.

text.p: A sweeping victory for Republican challenger Bob Dole in U.S. presidential elections on Tuesday would be the dream scenario for investors in Treasuries, analysts said on Monday.
But that is very unlikely to happen.
Instead, holders of T-bonds will be hoping for the best most analysts think they get -- no change at the White House, no change in the Senate, and no change in the House of Representatives.
"A landslide Republican victory would be the best possible outcome for T-bonds, " said Adrian Schmidt at Chase in London.

Adam Chester, international bond strategist at Yamaichi International, agreed, saying that if by some distant chance Dole did pull off a victory -- the 30-year long bond could gain a full point on the news.
"The markets would take it as a very positve step," he said. "But it isn't going to happen."
Latest opinion polls show that while President Bill Clinton's lead over Dole is dwindling slightly, he is still set to sail back to the oval office with relative ease.
The key pivot for the Treasury market will be the election outcome in the House of Representatives, analysts said.

"The House is touch and go," said Schmidt, an international economist. "If the Democrats won it, bonds would react badly because there would be underlying concern about a less restrictive budgetary policy."
But he said that some of those concerns were already priced into the market, and were probably the only thing blocking a potential move up in T-bond prices.
From a total of 435 seats in the House of Representatives, 430 are up for election this year.
Republicans currently hold a 235-197 majority and, with one seat already in hand, the Democrats need a net gain of 18 seats on Tuesday to recapture a clear majority.
"If the Republicans won (the house) Treasuries could surge quite sharply higher," said Schmidt.
Analysts said one of the major factors threatening that scenario was a risk of a low turnout at polling stations.
With Clinton's commanding lead over Dole in place for so long, this presidential campaign has been billed as one of the dullest ever, they said, and could leave many voters uninspired.
"The House of Representatives is the one which is really up for grabs," said Yamaichi's Chester. "And if there is a low turnout that could favour the Democrats.
He said that if Clinton's Democrats won either of the Congressional houses, the Treasury market would see a sharp setback, maybe losing as much as a point and a half on the news.
Michael Burke, bond strategist at Citibank, said the most likely reaction from the poll -- which he expects to return a "no change" status in U.S. politics -- would be Treasury prices drifting lower.

"Investors really haven't been particularly animated about the outcome of the election -- partly because they think it is a foregone conclusion, and partly because they dont believe that either a re-elected Clinton or a President Dole would mean a signficant change in policy," he said.

While Burke noted some market fears that Democrats taking control of Congress may lead to slight fiscal expansion, he said that with this year's budget deficit a modest $107 billion, the issue would not have too much of an adverse effect.
"Any reaction in the bond market is likely to be little more than a mild negative," Burke said.
-- Kate Kelland, International Bonds Unit +44 171 542 8682
